newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Thomson-CSF bids pit France against Europe.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Thomson-CSF bids pit France against Europe.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere Groupe on Wednesday submitted their final bids for the state's 58 percent stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF with Lagardere saying it had powerful British and German allies.

The sale of a majority in Thomson-CSF is the crucible for a European industry consolidation. The government is not expected to take any decision until after the two-round parliamentary election of May 25 and June 1.
Engineering group Alcatel Alsthom teamed up with private Dassault Industries and hopes state-owned Aerospatiale can link up in a later stage.

Against this French national-oriented grouping stands a more European approach from Lagardere, which said it had the "total and exclusive support" of two of Europe's biggest defence groups, Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa) and British Aerospace Plc.
GEC Plc said it had signed memoranda of understanding with both bidding groups.

The sale is being closely watched as France is the last of the four major European arms producers to shake up its industry, a step needed to open the way for new cross-border alliances with partners in Britain, Germany and Italy.

Lagardere, which is smaller than Alcatel in sales and market capitalisation, announced strategic cooperation accords with Dasa in space, missiles and defence electronics, and broke new ground with an agreement over naval systems with BAe.

In space, Lagardere's Matra Marconi Space joint venture with GEC will join Dasa to make a $3 billion business. In missiles, Lagardere's Matra BAe Dynamics venture will take 30 percent in Dasa's LFK unit. In defence electronics, Lagardere will combine certain areas in several steps to create a 50/50 joint venture with Dasa.

BAe said in London it was putting 300 million stg into Lagardere's offer via a 1.2 billion franc loan and by subscribing for 1.5 billion francs of a five-billion convertible bond, which Lagardere is issuing to help fund its Thomson-CSF bid.
Thomson-CSF made a 1996 net attributable profit of 745 million francs on sales of 36.3 billion francs.

Alcatel and Dassault, which holds a majority stake in warplane maker Dassault Aviation, said they were committed to increasing Thomson-CSF's size "by close to 50 percent to create a world leader in defence electronics, as well as in the associated civil sectors."

Dassault is offering to put its Dassault Electronique subsidiary into a joint venture with Thomson-CSF, which would bring significant assets in guidance systems, aircraft and missile electronics to Thomson-CSF.
If Aerospatiale joins up, that holds out the possibility of further integration as Aerospatiale is merging with Dassault Aviation, another move vital to the French consolidation.

Alcatel and Dassault said they could finance the acquisition from their own resources without compromising the future or using the resources of Thomson-CSF. It would form a 25 billion franc annual pool for research and development, with major benefits in civil and military synergies, the two companies said.

Lagardere said it had the means to fund the acquisition and eventually buy out Thomson-CSF minority shareholders. It would issue a special five billion franc bond convertible into Thomson-CSF shares to help fund the deal, along with its own cash and credit lines.
Alcatel shares closed 0.92 percent easier at 647 francs, while Lagardere was 2.22 percent lower at 176 francs. The CAC-40 blue-chip index closed down 0.33 percent.
